core_obligations: Forward implication: a dense open smooth over k meets the generic point of every irreducible component, so X is geometrically reduced at each such generic point, and the generic point criterion gives geometric reducedness of X (proof lines 4700-4707).

Converse, first reduction: discard the nowhere dense union of the pairwise intersections of irreducible components, so that X becomes a disjoint union of irreducible schemes and one may assume X irreducible (proof lines 4709-4714).

Converse, second step: an irreducible reduced scheme is integral, so at its generic point the local ring is the function field, which is geometrically reduced and hence separable over k; applying the separability-smoothness lemma to a nonempty affine open shows that some principal localization of its coordinate ring is smooth over k, giving the required dense smooth open (proof lines 4714-4726).
proof_roadmap: From a dense smooth open to geometric reducedness at generic points (proof lines 4700-4707).
Reduce to the irreducible case by removing pairwise intersections (proof lines 4709-4714).
Use separability of the function field to produce a smooth localization (proof lines 4714-4726).
difficulty_reason: For a reduced scheme X locally of finite type over a field k, the lemma proves that geometric reducedness is equivalent to the existence of a dense open subscheme smooth over k (statement lines 4693-4698). The forward implication uses that a dense smooth open contains the generic point of every irreducible component, where smoothness gives geometric reducedness, and then invokes the criterion that geometric reducedness can be checked at generic points (proof lines 4700-4707). The converse is a reduction: remove the nowhere dense union of the pairwise intersections of the irreducible components to make X a disjoint union of irreducibles, then use that an irreducible reduced scheme is integral, so that the structure sheaf at the generic point is the function field; geometric reducedness of that field makes it separable over k, and applying the separability-smoothness algebra lemma at the zero ideal shows that some principal localization of an affine chart is smooth, which is the required dense open (proof lines 4709-4726). The claim is H2: two standard input lemmas plus a reduction to the irreducible case, with the passage from a separable function field to smoothness of a localization as the key step.
